newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end up as fears of labour unrest fade.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end up as fears of labour unrest fade.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply higher on Thursday after recouping earlier losses caused by profit-taking, brokers said.
They said sentiment improved as fears of all-out strikes faded. Hopes foreign investors will return to the Seoul bourse also boosted buying.
The composite index ended at a provisional 711.86, up 1.73 percent or 12.10 points from Wednesday.
The index moved into negative territory in early afternoon trading due to profit-taking of blue chips but it shot up on a late buying spree, the brokers said.
"Buying was across the board as investors were confident the rally would continue a little longer," said Park Sang-woon of Seoul Securities.
Advancing stocks overwhelmed decliners by 772 to 90.
South Korea has been hit by wildcat strikes since the December 26 railroading of a controversial labour law, which allows employers to lay off workers and replace strikers.
Brokers said hopes were raised foreign investors would shift their attention to Asia because of talk about an imminent Wall Street fall.
Brokers said, however, buying would slow soon as the market was expected to face consolidation.
"The market will likely reach its short-term ceiling tomorrow at 720-730. I think the market cannot go like this without a pause," said Park of Seoul Securities.
The KOSPI-200 index added 0.88 of a point to 75.35, while its March futures contracts closed flat at 76.00.
